newsitem.title: INDIA: Delphi seeks 10 pct of India auto part market.
newsitem.headline: Delphi seeks 10 pct of India auto part market.

text.p: Delphi Automotive Systems, an affiliate of General Motors Corp, hopes to capture 10 percent of India's auto part market over the next five years, company officials said on Tuesday.
"There is a great potential here do a lot of things as the industry grows in India," J.T. Battenberg, president of Delphi Automotive Systems, told Reuters in an interview.
Delphi which obtained approval from the Indian government in 1995 to set up a wholly owned subsidiary, Delphi Automotive Systems Pvt Ltd, has five units producing auto components in India.
It currently produces fifteen to sixteen types of auto parts in India ranging from catalytic convertors to airconditioning and heating components, company officials said.
With many global car makers setting up base in India, the domestic auto component market was poised for high growth, Battenberg said.
India has attracted a clutch of foreign car makers ever since it began liberalising its economy in 1991.
Honda, Daewoo, Ford and Peugeot have set up car ventures in India.
Currently Delphi's major customers in India are Maruti Udyog, Daewoo, and General Motors, officials said.
Maruti Udyog Ltd, with a market share of 70 percent of the domestic market, is a 50:50 joint venture between government of India and Suzuki Motor Corp.
Delphi plans to cater to the domestic market as well exports.
"We have started exporting out of India already," said Battenberg
"Right now we have approved an investment of about $100 million (in India)," said William Ebert, president Asia-Pacific of Delphi Automotive Systems.
Ebert said he expected the Indian venture to post sales of about $100 million by 1997 and expected it to treble by 2001. He gave no sales figures for 1996.
Ebert said the Indian auto part market for the products in which Delhi is operating would grow to about $4.0 billion by 2001.
